core.title: Give every acceptance Given/When/Then prose and a verifiable outcome
core.given: A plan unit — a plan-artifact node that declares acceptance criteria — declares one or more acceptances.
core.when: The planner authors or edits an acceptance under that plan unit, or the confirmation phase (CONFIRM) validates every declared acceptance.
core.then: Each acceptance has present, non-empty Given/When/Then prose, and at least one Then line states a verifiable outcome a generated test can assert.
prefer: Write Given as the preconditions, When as the trigger action, and Then as the expected observable outcomes.
Phrase at least one Then line as a concrete, assertable observable outcome.
avoid: Leaving the Given, When or Then prose missing or empty.
Using a bare placeholder token (TBD, TODO, N/A) as the outcome — it is not a verifiable outcome.
Filling the fields with non-empty filler to pass the presence check while stating no assertable outcome.
Treating a well-formed acceptance as proof the plan unit's acceptance set is complete — this rule checks local shape only.
core.why: An acceptance whose narrative is missing, empty, or states no assertable outcome cannot be turned into a test, so its plan unit is unverifiable in practice while appearing covered on paper.
evidence: The realization's acceptance well-formedness check passes for every acceptance under every plan unit, with a fault-injection case proving missing Given/When/Then prose is caught.
On failure, the finding identifies the offending acceptance, the missing field, and its location.
verification: A presence check over each acceptance validates every acceptance declared under every plan unit: Given/When/Then prose present and non-empty, and at least one Then line states a verifiable outcome. The concrete schema traversal and the finding id belong to the realization.
Bare placeholder tokens (TBD, TODO, N/A) do not count as a verifiable outcome.
Enforced at the confirmation phase (CONFIRM), blocking it: every declared acceptance is validated, whether or not it was recently authored or edited. Severity 3; disposition strict.
On failure the finding reports the offending acceptance, the missing field, and its location; the exact report field names belong to the realization.
Scope is local shape only: whether a plan unit's acceptance set is complete is a separate coverage rule, not this check.

fires: The confirmation phase (CONFIRM) runs over a plan whose plan units declare acceptances, including existing, unchanged acceptances.
The planner adds a new acceptance under a plan unit in a plan artifact or product slice.
The planner edits an existing acceptance's Given/When/Then prose.
An acceptance's Then line is a placeholder such as TBD, TODO or N/A.
An acceptance has an empty or missing Given, When or Then narrative.
doesNotFire: Judging whether a plan unit has enough acceptances (set completeness) — that is the separate coverage rule.
Plan artifacts or plan units that declare no acceptances.
Outside the confirmation phase, edits to implementation code or tests that do not touch acceptance declarations (at CONFIRM all declared acceptances are still validated).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role, so the check can recognize the planning artifacts whose plan units declare acceptances.
The stack's local name for the acceptance-declaring plan unit that the core calls 'plan unit' (used in given/when/why/avoid and messages).

bunOnly.text: Validator conventions/presence/test_acceptance_well_formed passes for every acceptance under every WMBT node (fault-injection test: missing GWT prose is caught).
bunOnly.reason: Names this realization's validator ref and its fault-injection test; the core keeps the generic evidence (the check passes for every declared acceptance; a fault-injection case catches missing GWT prose).

bunOnly.text: On failure, the finding reports node_id, missing_field and node_location of the offending acceptance.
bunOnly.reason: The exact finding field names are this realization's report schema; the core keeps the neutral obligation to identify the offending acceptance, the missing field, and its location.

bunOnly.text: Validation family: presence; template: required_field_presence; variant: acceptance_well_formed; subject_kind: acceptance.
bunOnly.reason: Family/template/variant ids of this rule's validator are realization details (vocabulary notProfileKeys); the core describes the check generically as a presence check whose subject is the acceptance.

bunOnly.reason: The traversal names the Bun plan schema (wmbt nodes, acceptances[], the .abstract fields); the core keeps only the neutral selector 'every acceptance declared under every plan unit'.

bunOnly.text: Failure evidence fields: node_id, missing_field, node_location.
bunOnly.reason: Finding field names are this realization's report schema; the core states the reporting requirement generically.

bunOnly.text: Scope is local shape only; set completeness is checked by planner.coverage.every-wmbt-must-have.
bunOnly.reason: The cross-reference uses this stack's rule id; the core keeps the scope exclusion generically (set completeness is a separate coverage rule).

bunOnly.text: fact: finding, values: ["acceptance_well_formed"] — Missing/empty given/when/then.abstract or no verifiable then line is a validator finding.
bunOnly.reason: The finding id of this rule's validator is a realization detail; the core keeps a neutral finding value (acceptance_not_well_formed) for the same condition.

neutralityNotes: CONFIRM, Given/When/Then, 'acceptance' and 'a generated test' are ATDD-method vocabulary shared across stacks and are kept in the core. 'WMBT node' is neutralized to 'plan unit' with the stack's local name supplied by roles.plan_artifact.name, and the file kinds by roles.plan_artifact.kinds. Bun's 'wagon' grouping in activation.fires is generalized to 'plan artifact or product slice'. The acceptance-entry schema (traversal wmbt -> acceptances[] -> given/when/then.abstract, the .abstract field word) has no neutral equivalent and is bunOnly; likewise this rule's validator/family/template/variant/finding ids, the finding field names, and the sibling-rule id cross-reference. The placeholder token list (TBD, TODO, N/A) is treated as stack-neutral. No profile keys were missing, so proposedKeys is empty.
